decisions.title: Adoption of the @typing.override decorator proposal
decisions.summary: The `@typing.override` decorator was accepted with the name as proposed.
decisions.rationale: The name was chosen to be consistent with existing typing decorators and to clearly indicate the purpose of the decorator.

evidence.quote: The SC has decided to accept this PEP!

decisions.title: Compatibility with third-party libraries
decisions.summary: It was decided that a way to tell type checkers that a third-party library's `override` decorator should act like `@typing.override` is to use a `typing.TYPE_CHECKING` shim.
decisions.rationale: The approach was suggested by AlexWaygood and involves using a shim to make the third-party `override` decorator behave like `@typing.override` during type checking, while allowing for custom behavior at runtime.

decisions.title: Relationship with @abstractmethod
decisions.summary: The PEP recommends type checkers support a strict mode where all method overrides must be marked with the decorator, whether abstract or not.
decisions.rationale: The PEP recommends this to ensure consistency and clarity in method overriding, regardless of whether the method is abstract or not.

evidence.quote: I’m not sure there is much need for special treatment of abstract methods. The PEP recommends type checkers support a strict mode where all method overrides must be marked with the decorator, whether abstract or not.
evidence.author: a-reich
